title: Lean proofs that 178 best-known packings are local minima (n ≤ 324): registration request

body:
**Claim.** We derive the side of the register's best-known packing exactly, by a mechanical pipeline from its contact
graph, for 269 of the 324 counts. `S*_n` is the unique root of an explicit irreducible integer polynomial `p_n` in an
explicit rational interval `[a_n, b_n]`. An exact configuration over a number field `K_n = ℚ[t]/f_n` realises it, so
`s(n) ≤ S*_n` exactly. Each result is checked by an independent exact checker and, for 258 counts, by a Lean
proof of `Packs n S*_n`. These are the same packings as our certificates in #375 (T-098, T-101), so S' there is `S*`
rounded up.
- **176** have integer sides.
- **89** have a published closed form or polynomial, from David Ellsworth's page or this register's reported
  `exact_form` (for example `7 + 4/7` at n = 50, and the degree-672 polynomial at n = 83). Ours agrees with every one,
  and none disagrees. These may let the published forms move from reported to verified.
- **4 are new**: Francisco Couzo's recent packings, for which no exact form is published. At 102, 106 and 177,
  Ellsworth's page gives the polynomial of the earlier, larger packing (at 102, the Hajba/Cantrell/Ellsworth packing,
  `772s⁸ − 68416s⁷ + …`, root 10.6113879407752). Ours are for Couzo's improvements (at 102, root 10.6071746801761).
  The page has no form for 152.

  | n | deg p | field degree | coefficient size |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 102 | 8 | 8 | 13 digits |
  | 106 | 32 | 32 | 35 digits |
  | 152 | 40 | 40 | 52 digits |
  | 177 | 32 | 32 | 40 digits |

  n = 102: `22592x⁸ − 1740544x⁷ + 58564592x⁶ − 1123907648x⁵ + 13453474321x⁴ − 102847985308x³ + 490308874228x² −
  1332604124616x + 1580808833648`.

Open, 55 counts: n = 29, 55, 68, 71, 83, 88, … up to 307 (each listed in the table with its reason).

**Certificate.** `s12/search/exact/` at f58a017:
- `EXACT_FORMS.md` (table) and `exact_forms.json` (machine-readable): per n, `p` (ascending integer coefficients),
  `[a, b]`, `f`, field degree, and which checks passed.
- `minpoly/data/n-N.minpoly.json.gz`: the full exact form. It holds `f` and an isolating interval for its root `t*`, and
  each square's `x, y` and angle parameter `u = tan(θ/2)` as polynomials in `t` (`(c, s)` rational in `u`, so
  `c² + s² = 1` exactly). It also holds `S(t)`, `p` with `p(S(t)) ≡ 0 (mod f)`, and the contact list.
- `minpoly.py` derives them from the contact graph. It sorts the squares into angle classes, eliminates the centres,
  and uses msolve to parametrize when there is more than one class, with force balance (a Lagrange determinant) where
  the contacts leave a free direction. It then picks the root by exact real-root isolation (flint). The output is not
  trusted; see the checking section.

**Checking.**
- `verify_exact.py` uses only the standard library, with `Fraction` arithmetic. Every contact equation is checked as an
  identity mod `f`. Every other pair is checked as separated, and every corner as inside the box, by rational interval
  arithmetic at `t*`. It also checks `p(S) ≡ 0` and `S(t*) ∈ [a, b]`. `minpoly/verify_data.sh` replays all
  269: all 269 VALID, in about 3 minutes on 4 cores.
- Lean 4 / Mathlib `lean/Sqpack/ExactCheck.lean` and `ShadowCheck.lean`: `packs_exact` turns a certificate into
  `∃ s, p(s) = 0 ∧ a ≤ s ≤ b ∧ Packs n s`. `Packs` is the usual definition: closed unit squares in `[0, s]²` with
  pairwise disjoint interiors. The checks run by `decide +kernel`: field arithmetic mod `f` for contacts, and rational
  enclosures for every far or strictly separated pair and wall. There is no `native_decide`, and the axioms are
  `propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound`.
  - `lean_batch.py` generates and checks one proof per n: 258 of the 269, which is every one with field degree ≤ 20.
    The cost is about 8.4 hours of wall time summed over the records, with up to 2 chunks in parallel per record.
    The largest, at n ≈ 300, takes about 2.5 minutes of wall time on 4 processes.
  - The generated Lean files are not committed. `lean_batch.py --only N` rebuilds any of them from the data.
- Cross-checks: 86 agree and none differ. For low degree that's `mpmath.findpoly` on the 68-digit values; otherwise
  it's the degree, or the polynomial itself, on David Ellsworth's page (Kingbird) where it gives one. 12 of the page's
  polynomials describe a packing older than the current register record, so they don't apply.

**What the checkers share.** Same author and agent. `verify_exact.py` and the Lean generator read the same data file.
Their arithmetic and geometry are separate: `verify_exact.py` is Python `Fraction` code, and the Lean checker is a
kernel-checked program with a soundness proof. Neither trusts `minpoly.py` or msolve.

**Not done.**
- The open counts. 29, 68, 71, 126 and 228 need a polynomial system that msolve can't solve; for n = 29 we estimate the
  degree is above 120. 55 has a degree-85 force-balance determinant. 83 has degree 672 (Ellsworth and Chang give it).
  The rest of the 55 time out in msolve, need multi-direction force balance, or have fields of degree 56–144 (listed
  with reasons in the table). 292 has a certificate but no exact form yet.
- Lean proofs for field degree above 20 (41, 51, 69, 87, 106, 128, 152, 177, 205, 266, 300).
- Nothing here is about lower bounds. `S*` is the exact side of the known packing, not `s(n)`.

**Lineage and credit.** The packings are their finders' (the register's credits). Where Ellsworth publishes a
polynomial, ours agrees with it. The method of contact equations plus stationarity is his analytic approach; we
mechanised it from the contact graph and added the independent exact check and the Lean proofs. Register data: CC BY
4.0, Joshua Levy, the squares project.

**AI assistance.** The solver, checkers, Lean development and this batch were written with Claude (Anthropic) as a coding
and research agent, directed and reviewed by me.

body:
I would like to report two new preprints on the asymptotic deficiency c*(k) (k^2 - M(k), where M(k) is the largest number of unit squares in [0,k]^2 that are pairwise disjoint as closed sets). Both build on k2-minus-c version 1.2 (release v1.2, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23194031; paper doi:10.5281/zenodo.23194104), which addresses the findings of your review in #368 (RF-1 to RF-9; details in its README and reviews/REVIEWS.md). I mentioned v1.2 in a comment on #368, but since that issue is closed I am repeating it here.

1. Lower bound of order k^{1/4}
- Result: k^2 - M(k) >= 0.1 k^{1/4} for every integer k >= 4.62*10^12, and liminf (k^2 - M(k))/k^{1/4} >= 0.1696. Consequently s(k^2-c) = k for every integer k >= max(4.62*10^12, 10^4 c^4 + 1).
- Repository: https://github.com/squarepacker/k2-minus-c-quarter (release v1.0)
- DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23211207 (preprint, 108 pages, and programs)

2. Lower bound of order k^{1/3}
- Result: k^2 - M(k) > 10^-4 sqrt(k) for k in [10^8, 2.5*10^15], > 7*10^-5 sqrt(k) for k in [2.5*10^15, 3.5*10^17], and > 0.06 k^{1/3} for every integer k >= 3.5*10^17; liminf (k^2 - M(k))/k^{1/3} >= 0.06285. For every k >= 4.62*10^12 these bounds exceed the k^{1/4} bound above.
- Repository: https://github.com/squarepacker/k2-minus-c-cube-root (release v1.0)
- DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23212059 (preprint, 9 pages, and programs)
- The proof uses Sections 3-8 of the k^{1/4} preprint and Lemmas 4.13 and 4.15 of k2-minus-c as black boxes.

Dependence and status:
- The constants of both results rely on the computer-assisted Lemma 4.10 of k2-minus-c (the same lemma as in #368, whose box computations have not yet been reproduced by an independent implementation). Without it, both arguments still give power bounds with slightly smaller constants (k^{1/4}: 0.1 from 2.17*10^13 on, liminf 0.1411; k^{1/3}: 0.05 from 3.39*10^17 on, liminf 0.05229).
- Neither preprint has been peer reviewed. Each was checked by AI-based reviews, including a blank-slate review of the final text (no critical or major issue found; all minor issues addressed), by programs that recompute every displayed constant in interval and exact rational arithmetic, and by numerical tests on scaled analogues. Details are in reviews/REVIEWS.md of each repository.

If these fit your asymptotic waste bounds file, I would be grateful if you could consider them, and any review or comment would be very welcome.

Use of AI: developed with Claude (Anthropic), as described in each repository; I take full responsibility.

Sungjoon Ryu (@squarepacker)

body:
Prove that the Bidwell/Hämäläinen family is globally optimal for **17 unit squares with
independent rotations**, disjoint interiors, and boundary contact allowed:
$s(17)=S^\ast=4.67553009360455\ldots$. Deliver an explainer paper and a composed,
independently reviewable proof with exact certificates, replay instructions, and
explicit assurance limits.

This is the overall research tracker.
The proof remains open.

**Current integration status — October 9, 2026:**
[PR #475](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/pull/475) merged as
`0f16c033a87464cfab127ba54748ca5e2536babd`. Main now has **72 admitted entries**,
leaving **3,636 orbits / 28,528 states**, including **94 distance-2 orbits / 736
states**. Exp-317 admitted #472’s twelve certificates after listed-verifier FULL replay,
Rust parity, custody checks and review.
The endpoint survives; the numerical bound and open global proof obligations are
unchanged. The
[consolidated review record](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/pull/475#issuecomment-6090970439)
records all dispositions, review scopes, passing exact-head CI and the complete
twelve-job checkpoint.
The restricted family-cell checker is a scoped exact result, not global capture.
H-341 admission is complete; H-342 conversion, H-343 tail measurement and H-337/H-345
capture remain future work.

Here, $s(17)$ means the smallest container side that can hold seventeen unit squares.
A **lower bound** proves that every packing needs a larger container; an **upper bound**
comes from a construction that fits.
The goal is to make these meet at $S^\ast$, by ruling out every smaller packing.

The known construction and the local theorem are major ingredients, but the local
theorem applies only near the known family.
The missing global argument must show that every possible competing packing is either
impossible or reaches that theorem’s input region.
Eliminating one search case advances that argument without necessarily raising the
numerical lower bound.
The
[n17 explainer](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/docs/project/n17-optimality-explainer.md)
gives the case-specific argument;
[Tutorial §9](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/TUTORIAL.md#9-how-an-optimality-proof-is-built)
explains the general proof machinery.
The
[frontier case](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/packing/frontier/n-017.md),
[results register](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/packing/frontier/RESULTS.md),
and [assurance definitions](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/epistemics.md)
govern numerical claims and their verification/review status.

The explainer is a structural introduction; its dated narrative counts can lag the
census receipts and progress comments.
The
[Session184 proof-obligation review](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/ecb0bf82c38958089c7a41aa3980ce62dcc848b8/docs/project/reviews/review-2026-10-07-n17-session-184-progress.md)
and
[Session186 strategy](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/ecb0bf82c38958089c7a41aa3980ce62dcc848b8/docs/project/research/research-2026-10-07-n17-session-186-w3-strategy.md)
are research evidence landed with [PR404](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/pull/404)
(main `533dd42`), with their stated conditional premises and certification limits.
Browse the complete
[n17 issue](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3An-17) and
[PR](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/pulls?q=is%3Apr+label%3An-17) histories.

## Background: What the n = 11 Proof Established

Walter Trump’s 1979 eleven-square construction is now verified globally optimal:
$s(11)=T=(6u+4)/(1+2u-u^2)=3.877083590022814\ldots$, where $u$ is the unique root in
$(9/25,37/100)$ of $5u^8-10u^7-2u^6+14u^5+12u^4-6u^3+2u^2+2u-1$. The exact upper witness
T-011 and matching lower theorem T-060 settle the unrestricted problem.
T-060 stands at `V3/C3/S5`, machine-checked with its review record pending under the
current assurance ladder.
The [n11 case](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/packing/frontier/n-011.md)
records the claim and provenance.

The proof combines a complete closed centre cover and finite occupancy census, geometric
exclusions of all 2,180 nonterminal cases, capture through ten required nodes, exact
symmetry transfers, and local isolation at the algebraic endpoint.
Independent geometric executions and the reviewed composition close these obligations.
The publisher’s cached `RUN_ALL` route has four stale final-state digests; this
repository’s independent source-state replays establish T-060 separately.
The
[source packet](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/packing/resources/web/n11-optimality-2026-09-29/README.md),
[validation guide](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/packing/resources/web/n11-optimality-2026-09-29/VALIDATION.md),
and
[receipt guide](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/packing/resources/web/n11-optimality-2026-09-29/receipts/README.md)
distinguish fresh geometry, retained evidence checks, and composition.
Some exact arithmetic kernels are shared, and a fresh full replay needs the pinned bulk
objects and a reviewed receipt-rebinding workflow.

The reader-facing account is
[Paper III: Eleven-Square Optimality](https://jlevy.github.io/squares/papers/n11-optimality-review.html),
with its
[Markdown source](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/packing/devtools/templates/n11-optimality-review-article.md).
The earlier certificate lineage is explained in
[Paper I](https://jlevy.github.io/squares/papers/n11-lower-bounds-explainer.html)
([Markdown](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/packing/devtools/templates/n11-lower-bounds-explainer-article.md))
and [Paper II](https://jlevy.github.io/squares/papers/n11-threshold-bound-review.html)
([Markdown](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/packing/devtools/templates/n11-threshold-bound-review-article.md)):
fractional and threshold-charge certificates led to Kleddamag’s strict $s(11)>31/8$,
followed by Wang–Li’s slightly stronger strict bound.
Those bounds developed transferable tools, but equality required global exclusion,
capture and local geometry.

Local rigidity is a separate result: 128 branchwise tangent cones and the quantified
local-radius certificate do not alone establish global optimality.
T-112’s endpoint uniqueness corollary is recorded separately at `V3/C2/S3` in the
[n11 case](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/packing/frontier/n-011.md).
The reported
[Lean formalization](https://github.com/Queuingtheorydotcom/11SquaresFormalized) also
has a separate trust scope: it uses `native_decide` and trusts the compiler as well as
the kernel. This repository retains a scoped statement/construction build, not a fresh
complete build or human expert review of the full formalization.
See the
[statement audit](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/docs/project/reviews/review-2026-10-06-n11-lean-formalization-statement-audit.md)
and
[adversarial review](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/docs/project/reviews/review-2026-10-06-n11-lean-formalization-adversarial.md).

## n = 17: Results and Proof Architecture

The verified bracket, with changes recorded in dated updates, is
$4.66044275<s(17)\le4.6755300936045509516342148538535054$. Guzhou0806 / N17 project’s
R071 lower bound (T-093, `V3/C3`) continues the weighted-charge lineage of earlier Mira,
Kleddamag and Guzhou bounds; its paired C++ and Node replays use the same event-cell
method. See the
[R071 proof review](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/docs/project/reviews/review-2026-10-05-guzhou-r071.md).
The unchanged charge has an obstruction at $4.660442775$, leaving only
$2.5\times10^{-8}$ additional runway; this limits that method, not the true optimum.
For the chronology of verified lower-bound improvements and the significance of recent
intermediate results, see the dated progress comments below.
The official
[results register](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/packing/frontier/RESULTS.md)
and
[source records](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/packing/frontier/results.yaml)
already retain the successive lower bounds as T-041, T-043 and T-093. A stronger
numerical claim gets a new T-item under the
[result-import procedure](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/packing/campaign/result-import.md#stage-3-record);
it moves the verified case bound only when the required proof checks and review are
complete. Additional evidence for an existing claim updates that item.
Partial case exclusions, conditional restrictions and verifier improvements have their
own research records and do not constitute a new numerical lower bound.

The known upper construction has ten axis-aligned squares, six at one nontrivial tilt
and one at another. Three squares slide and square 6 moves in its hole: the target is a
family. Exact endpoint feasibility (T-065) and the identity with the irreducible
degree-18 catalogue polynomial are accepted;
[exp-245](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/packing/campaign/series/series-000-smoke-and-calibration/experiments/exp-245-h265-n17-catalogue-polynomial.md)
closes the side-identity obligation.
Feasibility supplies an upper bound, not optimality.

The selected architecture adapts n11’s decomposition:

The cover divides the possible square-centre locations into named regions.
A **state** assigns the seventeen squares to these regions; an **orbit** groups states
that differ only by a rotation or reflection of the container.
An **admitted exclusion** is a fully verified proof ruling out its declared cases.
**Capture** means proving that a surviving case lies inside the local theorem’s complete
input region. These terms describe proof obligations, rather than numerical improvements
to the bound.

| Obligation | Established ingredient | Completion requirement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global cover and assignment | [exp-247](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/packing/campaign/series/series-000-smoke-and-calibration/experiments/exp-247-h266-n17-unique-state-cover.md): 24 closed capacity-one cells, 346,104 states / 43,593 D4 orbits; the entire endpoint family occupies one state | Preserve closed seams, symmetry, state labels and cap semantics in every consumer and branch refinement. |
| Exclude other states | Ownership-induction and interval branch-and-bound certificates, admitted only after full standing verification | Exclude every remaining nonterminal state at a certified cap at least $S^\ast$; heuristic selector flags and numerical failures receive no exclusion credit. |
| Capture the surviving state | Retained kernel pilots and capture analyses | Prove reach from the actual cells to the terminal theorem’s complete input region, with compatible frame, angle charts and cap. A successful small-box contraction alone does not prove this. |
| Local family theorem | Common-core stress, coordinate duals, nonlinear bounds and slider coverage: [local recipe](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/docs/project/reviews/review-2026-10-02-n17-local-theorem-recipe.md), [composition](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/docs/project/reviews/review-2026-10-02-n17-local-half-composition.md) | The usable theorem assumes the known state and 45 non-slider coordinates within $1/5000$ in its specified frame. It composes machine-certified parts and reviewed hand lemmas 1–6; end-to-end machine checking is not claimed. Broader H-261 remains unresolved as worded. |
| Compose and publish | Exact endpoint, cover, admitted ledger, receipts and checker tools | Close every interface and unresolved premise; provide portable certificate custody, replay evidence, and an explainer whose claims match the proof. |

The exclusion census cap is $U=1169/250=4.676$. Capture uses a much tighter rational
outer cap $U'$ enclosing $S^\ast$, with $0<U'-S^\ast\le10^{-12}$, while retaining the
cover’s frame. Each terminal leaf must prove the local theorem’s complete premises for
target packings of side at most $S^\ast$; arbitrary feasible points in the outer $U'$
relaxation need not satisfy the local theorem’s original-containment premise.
Monotonicity, centring and root-enclosure allowances must be proved at the joins.
The
[n17 explainer](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/docs/project/n17-optimality-explainer.md)
and
[X-048 exploration](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/packing/campaign/explorations/X-048-n17-optimality-after-n11.md)
retain the alternate routes, diagnostic failures and precise mathematical interfaces.

## Workstreams and Evidence Admission

| Workstream | Coordination | Proof or integration obligation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Complete exclusions and global capture | This tracker; current survey and plan [X-052](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/pull/475) | Preserve the global cover and compose full exclusions or reach into the local family’s complete input region. The two open gaps are excluding the residual nonterminal states and capture from the family’s actual cells. Use the dated census for counts; bounded stalls do not establish impossibility of an architecture. |
| External sub-pattern certificates | [#358](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/issues/358), [#413](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/issues/413) (38 rows), [#472](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/issues/472) (12 native kernel certificates) | Acquire complete packages, perform standing FULL replay under a listed verifier and establish exact marginal census coverage. #472’s exp-317 admission landed in #475, removing 1,047 orbits relative to the prior 60-entry baseline. The remaining #413 rows retain their own admission obligations. |
| Producer branching | [#367](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/issues/367) | Reproducible B2/B2d changes and controlled downstream replay; smaller search trees do not establish proof acceptance. |
| Branch-and-bound verification | [#400](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/issues/400); [#445](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/issues/445) closed by #452 | Preserve all completeness and parent-child induction checks through native, parallel and memory-lifetime changes. |
| Kernel verifier | [PR410](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/pull/410) | Same-object full parity, provenance/admission integration and atomic receipts; ordinary-container hull-16 support does not replace centered hull-48 replay. |
| Held construction and algebraic sources | [#375](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/issues/375), [#419](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/issues/419), [PR403](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/pull/403), [PR435](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/pull/435) | Keep source-reported exact forms, independently checked feasibility, algebraic identity, local minima and global optimality separate. |

An external certificate becomes an admitted exclusion only after its exact named cells,
cover, frame, cap, complete independent closed-angle domain and boundary convention are
joined to immutable certificate objects and complete standing-verifier receipts.
Any narrower guards must be discharged.
The canonical D4 join determines duplication and marginal census coverage.
Author-reported closure, fast-only verification, compact-header acceptance and projected
orbit counts remain separate evidence levels.
Partial computation or resource exhaustion earns no exclusion credit.
Bulk certificates stay outside Git with retained manifests and reproducible acquisition
instructions; source provenance and generated-object identity have distinct roles.

**Conditional geometric propagation:** Widened inequalities, strict-core transfer,
owned-hull restrictions and closed centre branching can strengthen consequences inside
declared guards. Their composition must retain every centre, angle, root and slider
premise. A restricted child or surviving relaxation does not establish reach into its
guard, whole-parent infeasibility or global capture.
The accepted numeric cap $V=935106018721/200000000000$ lies above the certified
endpoint; the
[cap join](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/ecb0bf82c38958089c7a41aa3980ce62dcc848b8/packing/campaign/series/series-000-smoke-and-calibration/experiments/exp-275-h288-capture-cap-root-join.md)
resolves that interface only.

**Shared-centre relaxation:** Couple pairwise incircle constraints through one common
vector of seventeen centres, reconstructing all region and pair rows exactly.
The
[first-eight P8 contract](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/docs/project/research/research-2026-10-07-n17-shared-centre-lp-readiness.md)
requires a separate exact feasible endpoint control.
For reconstructed $Ax\le b$, nonnegative rational multipliers satisfying $A^Ty=0$ and
$b^Ty<0$ certify infeasibility of the selected relaxation; ordinary admission still
requires composition and deduplication checks.
An exact primal establishes survival of that encoded relaxation, not a physical packing.
Numerical solver status supplies neither certificate.
This route does not replace the whole-square or capture obligations.

The exact endpoint calibration now reconstructs all seventeen cell domains, all 136 pair
domains and the common rational centre vector in a fresh process, under the explicit
`f1` frame action. The
[exp316 record](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/2c3e00321a4302b43dc19f0a3578fc92a1329c1c/packing/campaign/series/series-000-smoke-and-calibration/experiments/exp-316-h-324-shared-centre-explicit-f1.md)
and [PR461](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/pull/461) retain the calibration and its
resource limits. This establishes a positive control for the relaxation checker.
It does not exclude an ordinary assignment, admit an exclusion, raise a bound or prove
optimality. A numerical candidate in the first-eight pilot must still undergo exact
reconstruction and independent checking.
Singular or failed reconstruction remains unresolved; resource exhaustion is incomplete.
Neither provides an exclusion certificate.
The W2 review of
[X-051](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/packing/campaign/explorations/X-051-n17-optimality-program-review.md)
§3.1 found exact rational centres in each first-eight state’s own cells, pairwise at
least 1 apart and accepted by the repository’s checker, and the same for all 95
distance-2 orbits.
So this relaxation excludes none of them; that is relaxation survival,
not a packing or an exclusion.

**Verification changes:** A memory-lifetime repair for retained BB internal nodes must
preserve every parent-child induction check, completeness condition and certificate/
receipt identity join.
A merged verifier or passing engineering controls does not admit a mathematical
certificate. Runtime gains require measurements on the actual consumer path, with the
proof criteria and refusal controls unchanged.

## Exact Optimization Certificates and Research Selection

The
[Astra strategy review](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/3ec6e7df84bc40385e0dd8c3804b69acad5fb7a4/docs/project/reviews/review-2026-10-08-n17-strategy-and-exact-sos.md)
explains how joint geometry, sum-of-squares certificates and exactification fit this
proof architecture. Its experiments and resource limits are proposals, not executed
results. [Maaz’s Sostactic article](https://www.mmaaz.ca/writings/sostactic.html)
provides the numerical-SDP-to-exact-certificate approach under investigation.

A shared-centre LP preserves one vector of seventeen centres across all 136 square
pairs. An exact feasible primal establishes survival of that relaxation; exact Farkas
multipliers establish a contradiction only after the original-cell and cap premises are
joined. Pairwise feasible witnesses cannot substitute for one common centre vector.
Endpoint feasibility is a required positive control.

A scoped sum-of-squares (SOS) certificate can preserve nonlinear constraints among
several owners. For inequalities $g_i(z)\ge0$ and equalities $h_j(z)=0$, a checked
identity $-1=\sigma_0+\sum_i\sigma_i g_i+\sum_j\lambda_j h_j$, with each $\sigma_i$ a
nonnegative weighted sum of squares, proves the encoded system empty.
Numeric SDP status is not this proof.
Exact coefficient identities, nonnegative weights, complete premises and an independent
fresh checker are required.
Singular Gram matrices may make rational reconstruction fail even when a numerical
candidate looks promising.
Failed reconstruction remains unresolved.
A resource stop is incomplete and supplies no mathematical verdict.

The
[three-source mathematical review](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/51368bec05b6fa30bebca7b31d0cf3dd0d810c09/docs/project/reviews/review-2026-10-08-n17-global-optimization-and-sos.md)
connects Berthold et al.'s packing formulations, Blekherman–Parrilo–Thomas’s positivity
theory and Laplagne’s exact singular-Gram recovery methods to this architecture.
For a triple of original closed cell domains, its derived weighted-vertex screen
replaces an unconditional order-2 SDP attempt in the specified no-ball/no-equality
incircle ansatz. Exact positive weights can exclude the triple directly; an exact
normalized mixture obstruction rules out every contradiction in that particular recipe.
A mixture is not a feasible physical triple, and numerical failure remains inconclusive.
A rational-ball augmentation requires a separate frozen recipe and exact containment on
the entire original product domain; reduced higher-order recipes remain subject to their
actual facet counts and resource caps.
These analytical reductions retain the original-cell/D4 composition obligations.
On the 24-cell cover this screen cannot act: X-051 §3.2, checked exactly by its W2
review, finds a feasible product vertex for each of the 2,024 cell triples, so no
weighted-vertex certificate exists and no SOS infeasibility certificate exists for any
triple at any order, with or without the ball augmentation.

The unrestricted packing problem is a finite disjunction of nonconvex quadratic systems:
every pair needs one of the separating-axis alternatives, with touching boundaries
retained. A single guessed contact branch or centre-distance relaxation does not cover
this disjunction. Global optimality at the algebraic endpoint also requires the correct
ordered root, rather than a rounded rational substitute.
The existing exact branch-and-bound verifier already checks interval subdivisions; a
multi-owner SOS leaf would add a joint polynomial obstruction within that framework.
Select and calibrate a small original-cell pilot before allocating a dense global SDP.

## Bead Work Map

Beads track deliverables and dependencies; dated comments record current heads, checks,
findings and execution outcomes.
Existing lanes continue through these anchors, without duplicating other owners’ work:

| Obligation | Beads | Evidence and coordination |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Program selection | `think-knii`, `think-a1fv` | X-051 is merged in #473; X-052 and its mathematical corrections landed in #475. Survey bead think-knii is complete; future W10 selection belongs to the open program think-tmz6, with H-341 admission complete. |
| #472 admission and integration | `think-6p3d` (H-341), `think-n53s` | exp-317 records listed FULL replay, Rust parity and custody for twelve object pairs merged through #475. Admission review, integration checks and landing are complete; think-6p3d is complete and durable parity-tool follow-up think-n53s remains separate under the open program. |
| Hard tail and capture | `think-j6qy`, `think-juy9`, `think-g2qn` | H-343 measures the remaining tail; H-337 and H-345 test capture from the required starting domains. A merged hull repair does not mean these target runs executed. |
| Answered relaxation pilots | `think-dvcs`, `think-geid` | Merged X-051 supplies eight exact shared-centre survivors and feasible vertices for all 2,024 triples in the specified weighted-vertex/SOS recipe. Their specified recipes have known negative outcomes; retire or redirect dispositions await owner review. Stronger models need separate scoped proposals. |
| Held evidence and replay guard | `think-yg80`, `think-b0ef` | Held closures await disposition; the RSS-query repair and maintained C2 replay remain distinct from merged #452. |
| Custody and proof package | `think-jhgi`, `think-1111` | #475 hosts its 24 new objects. The older 204-object custody gap, missing Session 184 tags and tracked bulk-data disposition remain separate obligations. |
| Catalogue integration | `think-70h9`, `think-okxn`; owners `think-jygq` / `think-wuol` | Open #403 → #435; their exact-head check status is in dated updates. The earlier #450 intake has merged. |
| Contributor acquisition and applicability | `think-ewea`, `think-bmwd`, `think-n01y`, `think-t41a`, `think-kk7w`, `think-x4v4`, `think-00e3`, `think-8sm2` | #413, #358, #472, #400, #375 and #419 retain distinct producer, custody, replay, catalogue and admission scopes. See each issue’s current status note. |
| Record hygiene and worker inputs | `think-yjgk`, `think-t1lk` | Keep the T-065 wording and worker-input selection follow-ups separate from mathematical progress. |

The overarching program remains BC-418 / `think-tmz6`. Continue from the latest dated
decision and linked deliverables rather than its historical session framing.

## Progress and Closure

BC-418 / `think-tmz6` owns the program.
Dated comments maintain the current state: verified results and admitted census,
negative or inconclusive experiments, held evidence, active owners, planned work, and
the next proof obligation.
Each update links immutable evidence or identifies a moving source revision, states what
ran, and distinguishes plans from executions.
Update the body when the objective, proof architecture or durable background changes;
record ordinary progress in comments.
Keep counts, experiment outcomes, CI verdicts, current owners and integration blockers
in dated comments, distinguishing merged main, verified work on open branches and
external reports. Link related issues rather than closing distinct producer, verifier,
custody or mathematical obligations as duplicates.

Close this tracker only when a composed proof covers every packing and establishes
$s(17)=S^\ast$, all required certificates are fully verified, all frame/cap/state/slider
joins are discharged, and the explainer and replay package accurately disclose their
assurance and remaining portability limits.

## Accepted Results and Remaining Exclusions

  obstruction leaves $2.5\times10^{-8}$ of method runway.
  See the

  duals and nonlinear bounds on the declared slider box; exp-248 composes slider
  coverage. The capture-target theorem assumes the known occupancy state, its declared
  frame, and all 45 non-slider coordinates within $1/5000$. It composes
  machine-certified components with reviewed hand lemmas 1–6. H-261’s broader slider
  claim remains unresolved; these results do not supply global capture.
  See the
  [composition review](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/ef79288a498b5469e6b944f7b150d83aeeab5f94/docs/project/reviews/review-2026-10-02-n17-local-half-composition.md).

## Capture and Alternate Terminal Theorem

Pilot 2 continued small contractions but met its falsifier: no two-sided position extent
fell by ten percent once every widest row was below $1/20$ of its extent.
[Capture R9](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/ef79288a498b5469e6b944f7b150d83aeeab5f94/docs/project/reviews/review-2026-10-05-n17-capture-r9.md)

competing readings. Compression repair `think-juy9` already has an external executor,
`guzhou-codex-graph-gate`, working on a prepended $2^{-18}$ fine candidate with the
exact checks and fallback preserved.
Repairing that floor does not itself predict contraction.

round-15 worst position extent at most 0.5 of baseline supports readiness; at least 0.9
refuses n17 interpretation; the middle is inconclusive.
Synthetic recession and known-case contraction are separate controls.

rebuilt using the **same repaired producer**. Freeze side-W2’s into-wall turn side and
side-N0/side-N2’s full turn ranges; verify that actual angular refinement occurred.
Proposed falls of at least 20% and 40% support the row-driven reading; all three ranges
within 5% at fourfold rows support the box-set reading.
Mixed/intermediate outcomes remain inconclusive.
Any terminal theorem still requires a separate cells-to-region capture proof.

R9 stage 1 is sequential: historical costs are roughly 35,000 seconds to rebuild round
17 and 20–22 CPU-hours overall.
Extra cores do not make a ten-hour verdict available.
A full scaling target should wait for measured readiness and cost; a preparation
checkpoint must be labelled incomplete.

Cheap widened finite-angle LP reconnaissance is selected alongside repair/control, ahead
of costly scaling. The old `lp_probe` scratch instrument is absent and was not retained:
build a reviewed instrument and endpoint/branch/slider controls first.
The
[widened-projection scope](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/ef79288a498b5469e6b944f7b150d83aeeab5f94/docs/project/reviews/review-2026-10-02-n17-widened-projection-scope.md)
is a candidate contract, not a theorem.
For a fixed feature branch, its value is the supremum of feasible dual lower bounds; an
outer minimum ranges over allowed feature branches.
A bad sampled sheet does not refute the primal claim.
One point can require up to $2^9=512$ branch LPs: 8,000 direction/radius points are not
8,000 solves. Sampled basis counts estimate reconnaissance cost and certify no
directional coverage.
Freeze the patch threshold and degenerate-estimator behavior before a newly registered
target.

## Tail, Assurance and Custody

The retained residue survey describes historical 5,084/2,256 selector populations at
arities seven/eight.
Extend it against the admitted ledger before claiming actual-tail strata.
Classify genuine fixed points, cap stalls, near-endpoint states, untested cases and
missing diagnostics; charge production, self-check, full verification and storage

The paper supplies polynomial non-overlap formulations used with SCIP/Xpress. Polynomial encoding is feasible, but numerical SDP output still needs exact coefficient identities, nonnegative square decompositions and complete coverage of the claimed cells.

**No solver target ran and no bound changed:** `4.66044275 < s(17) <= 4.6755300936045509516342148538535054`. Focused documentation/math-format checks pass. One broad push-validation attempt failed, with environment, nested-control and unchanged snapshot-cap failures disclosed on the draft; hosted checks are pending. This literature assessment does not qualify the earlier stack as merge-ready.

## SOS source review and analytical reduction — October 8, 2026

[PR464](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/pull/464) now extends the existing review with the Blekherman–Parrilo–Thomas book and [Laplagne's facial-reduction paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.04215v1). Sol checked full raw coverage (487/19 PDF pages) and extraction defects; original PDF pages and Laplagne's original TeX support the consequential readings. The full book remains outside Git; source identity/quality and the small Laplagne sources are retained. No whole-source corrected mathematical transcription is claimed.

**Astra derived and reviewed a new conditional simplification:** with exactly affine cell facets, three incircle generators and no equality terms or quadratic ball, every order-2 SOS contradiction supplies a strict weighted-vertex certificate. An exact LP over three nonnegative normalized weights can therefore exclude the triple directly. An exact vertex-mixture obstruction rules out that entire SOS recipe; it is not a feasible packing. The proof and source locators are in the [extended review](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/fed171802307da9e7b2f6b2bd93d145d39f128ac/docs/project/reviews/review-2026-10-08-n17-global-optimization-and-sos.md).

The same forced-face proof reduces the twelve-facet order-2 system to 367 Gram unknowns and 30,828 dense entries. Reduced order 3 still exceeds the cap at twelve facets, but can pass this count at nine. A separately frozen rational ball, checked to cover the original domain, gives an eligible order-2 alternative (854 unknowns / 179,340 entries at twelve facets). These are analytical sizes, not measured solver outcomes.

The selected sequence is unchanged at its entry: `think-dvcs` first-eight shared-centre LP, then equal-weight vertices, exact weighted vertices and a separately specified SOS successor under revised `think-geid`. Source-and-controls readiness must verify the face exposure/embedding, complete vertices, exact primal/mixture decisions, rational ball coverage, touching/endpoint and resource controls.

**No target ran, no case was excluded and no bound moved.** The bracket remains `4.66044275 < s(17) <= 4.6755300936045509516342148538535054`; no T-item is claimed. Focused documentation/math/source-preservation checks pass. The previous broad validation failure remains disclosed; PR464 is a draft and does not qualify the older stack for merging.

### What the mathematical work changes

The ordinary census still has **60 admissions, 36,768 surviving states and 4,683 D4
orbits**. The difficult subset is **95 orbits/744 states**, not the whole remaining
proof obligation. The first-eight shared-centre LP remains **unimplemented, unregistered
and unrun**. Endpoint feasibility demonstrates that the exact adapter accepts its

The updated strategy is: first implement and preregister that LP with exact primal or
Farkas verification; then apply the exact weighted-vertex screen to a frozen survivor.
That screen replaces the previously proposed unconditional no-ball order-2 SDP pilot.
An exact positive weighted inequality may exclude its domain directly; an exact
normalized mixture may rule out every contradiction in the specified no-ball/no-equality
ansatz for that triple.
A mixture is not a physical packing, and numerical failure is inconclusive.
Ball-augmented order 2 or a reduced order-3 successor needs separate preregistration,
verified domain containment, actual facet/cap constraints and all original-cell/D4
joins. These are analytical recommendations; no new target solver experiment has run.

the first eight. All 35 reconciled contributor classes, including #358’s two, remain
unadmitted. Complete object/receipt custody, full standing replay, original-domain joins
and deduplication are still required.
Neither these reports nor faster verification changes the census or bound by itself.

Keep the remaining global coverage, capture and local-theorem interface obligations
explicit. Landing useful documentation and tools does not close them.
The broader snapshot-selection work remains `think-t1lk`; the narrow 192 MiB repair does
not complete it. No new full workflow, proof-search campaign, merge or draft promotion
was initiated during this reconciliation.

body:
**Maintainer status — October 9, 2026:** The standing BB verifier’s memory-lifetime
repair #452 is merged and closes #445. The measurements below describe the earlier
verifier and remain historical benchmark evidence.
Adoption of the proposed parallel or Rust BB paths, current-verifier receipt parity,
custody and certificate admission remain separate open work.
The ordinary-container Rust **kernel** verifier in #410 is a different checker; its
merge does not adopt these BB tools.
See the
[latest integration checkpoint](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/issues/400#issuecomment-6077613717)
and overall tracker #405.

* * *

This reports two tools that check `n17-subpattern-bb-certificate/v1` certificates faster
than the standing verifier, `packing/devtools/verify_n17_bb_certificate.py`, with the
same verdicts and the same receipts.
Whether to use either is for this repository to decide.

## Why this may matter here

Section 6 of `docs/project/reviews/review-2026-10-02-n17-cost-reduction-performance.md`
puts re-verification after a checker change at 1,000 to 3,000 CPU-hours per change.
It also expects 100 to 300 after the planned rate steps.
The standing verifier is a single process.
Its memory grows with the tree: 10.6 GB on the 194,328-node certificate below.
Both tools here act on that cost.

## The two tools

1. **A parallel driver for the standing verifier** (`verify_n17_bb_parallel`). It
   imports `verify_n17_bb_certificate` unchanged.
   It runs that module’s header, trigonometry and tree checks (T1 to T3) once, as
   `run_checks` does. Then it hands whole chunks to worker processes, and each worker
   calls the module’s own `Verifier.check_node` on every node of its chunks.
   - `check_node` reads one thing from a parent: its final boxes.
     Each worker takes them from the pass-1 index and also confirms that a node’s
     `final` equals the indexed copy.
   - The standing verifier requires a parent’s chunk to come no later than its child’s.
     The driver keeps that requirement as a check.
   - The receipt has the standing verifier’s fields and counters, plus a `parallel`
     entry.
   - It is about 200 lines.
     We can open it as a pull request if it is wanted.
2. **An independent Rust verifier**, published as `n17_bb_verifier/` in
   [wand125/square-packing-tools](https://github.com/wand125/square-packing-tools).
   - It was written from the standing verifier and the certificate README, used as the
     specification. It shares no code with the standing verifier, the generator or the
     native kernel.
   - It decides with exact rationals (`rug`/GMP); floating point is used only for
     timing.
   - Its receipts carry the standing verifier’s fields and per-check counters.
   - Its first pass interns repeated JSON subvalues of the tree, so memory per node is
     about a quarter of its first version.
   - Its tests include six corrupted copies of a small certificate (a multiplier, a
     tightened bound, a cut’s right side, an angle split point, a dropped leaf, a
     narrowed final box).
     Each must fail at the matching check, as in the standing verifier.

## Benchmark

All runs were on one host, one run at a time, each under `/usr/bin/time -v`:

- Host: GCE `c2d-highcpu-8` (AMD EPYC 7B13, 8 vCPU, 15 GB), Linux 7.0.0-1011-gcp, Python
  3.14.7.
- Standing verifier: `verify_n17_bb_certificate.py`, byte-identical to `main` (SHA-256
  `9dcc05bc…`).
- Parallel driver: SHA-256 `1cc5c15d…`, on top of `main`’s verifier.
- Rust verifier: “first version” is the original commit, and “compact” is the published
  version.

“Agrees” means the receipt equals the standing verifier’s on `status`, `nodes`,
`closed_leaves`, `reasons`, `max_depth`, `checked_nodes`, `node_failures`, every entry
of `counts`, and `failure_count`.

| Certificate | Nodes | Objects | Standing, 1 process: wall / CPU / peak RSS | Parallel driver, 8 processes: wall / CPU / peak RSS | Rust, first version, 8 threads: wall / CPU / peak RSS | Rust, compact, 8 threads: wall / CPU / peak RSS |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A (B2 rule) | 30,822 | 64 | 727 s / 725 s / 1.32 GB | 159 s / 1,153 s / 0.25 GB, agrees | 19.7 s / 110 s / 0.18 GB, agrees | 19.8 s / 111 s / 0.07 GB, agrees |
| side-S0, side-W0 + 5 interior (B2) | 79,396 | 161 | 2,177 s / 2,173 s / 4.11 GB | 453 s / 3,491 s / 0.51 GB, agrees | 61.6 s / 327 s / 0.44 GB, agrees | 59.5 s / 327 s / 0.11 GB, agrees |
| side-S0, side-N0 + 5 interior (B2) | 194,328 | 391 | 6,073 s / 6,066 s / 10.6 GB | 1,229 s / 9,505 s / 1.10 GB, agrees | 157 s / 814 s / 1.00 GB, agrees | 153 s / 814 s / 0.22 GB, agrees |
| side-W0, side-W2 + SW, NW, W, S, N (B2d) | 924,233 | 1,851 | not run: over this host’s memory | not run: 8 processes exceeded 15 GB | 1,153 s / 5,488 s / 5.03 GB | 1,134 s / 5,480 s / 1.20 GB, receipts equal to the first version |

- Peak RSS is what `/usr/bin/time -v` reports: the largest single process among the
  run’s processes.
- On the three certificates the standing verifier could check, the compact Rust verifier
  is 37 to 40 times faster in wall time on 8 threads, and 6.5 to 7.5 times faster in CPU
  time. It also uses 19 to 48 times less memory.
- The parallel driver is 4.6 to 4.9 times faster in wall time on 8 processes.
  Its total CPU is about 1.6 times the single process’s.

### Commands

From `packing/`:

```bash
python -m devtools.verify_n17_bb_certificate CERT --output standing.json
python -m devtools.verify_n17_bb_parallel CERT --processes 8 --output parallel.json
n17bb-verify CERT --threads 8 --output rust.json
```

## Limits

- These are single runs on one host type.
- The Rust verifier checks the non-Taylor `/v1` schema that this repository’s
  certificates use. It does not check the Taylor variant, or a cover’s capacity or
  completeness.
- It also checks a `/v3` extension that we wrote for our own certificates: angle
  tightening (`tighten` splits and `closed: "angle"` leaves).
  That extension is not part of this repository’s schema, and the standing verifier does
  not check it. It is mentioned only to state the tool’s scope; the benchmark above uses
  `/v1` certificates only.
- The parallel driver needs enough memory for the standing verifier’s pass-1 index in
  the parent. Each worker also holds a copy as it reads parent final boxes, so 8 workers
  did not fit in 15 GB for the 924,233-node certificate.
- The two B2 flagged-class certificates are those reported in #358 and hosted at
  wand125/n17-certificates.
  The A and B2d certificates are not hosted.

body:
Following `packing/frontier/README.md#adding-or-reviewing-a-result`.

**Claim.** For 48 counts n, `s(n) ≤ S'_n`, where each `S'_n` is a rational slightly below the register's current reported
bound: by 3e-13 to 5e-11. These are not new packings. Each is the exact optimum of the register's own known-best packing,
mostly Francisco Couzo's of 27 September and 3 October, with the f64 slack removed. The counts are
68, 102, 103, 106, 110, 123, 126, 131, 132, 152, 154, 155, 156, 172, 177, 180, 181, 182, 199, 206, 207, 208, 209, 210, 211, 228, 236–241, 259, 263, 268–273, 297, 301–307. The table, with the register value, our `S'` and the difference, is `results.md` in the bundle.

We ran the same pipeline on every register record, n = 1–324, so the bundle also holds exact certificates for 321 of
them, including every n ≤ 104. For the 273 that don't improve, S' is above the register's printed value by 1e-20 to
1e-14 (the printed values are rounded to 15–16 digits). That may be useful as an
independent exact replay of the existing upper bounds. We don't ask for anything to be registered from the 273 that
don't improve.

**Certificate.** `s12/search/exact/batch/` in https://github.com/evand/square-packing (commit [13ee36e](https://github.com/evand/square-packing/tree/13ee36e5807727d12a5da36b9b90a96bdba272bf/s12/search/exact/batch)).
`certs/n-N.cert` is a rational packing: n unit squares given by rational centres and rational `t = tan(θ/2)`, so
`(c, s) = ((1−t²)/(1+t²), 2t/(1+t²))` holds exactly, inside an open box of rational side `S'`. The format is in
`../README.md` (§ Certificate). `inputs/n-N.txt` is the f64 packing each certificate was solved from. 37 of the 48
improvements start from the register witness directly. The other 11 start from that witness after a local squeeze
(our SLP optimizer, not yet published), which matters only for reproducing the solve, not for checking the certificate.

**Checking.**
- `verify_cert.py`: exact rationals (stdlib `Fraction`). Each square is checked strictly inside the box. Each pair
  with centre distance² ≤ 2 is checked as separated along one of the 4 face normals; the other pairs by disjoint
  circumscribed discs.
- `verify_cert2.py`: exact rationals, a different method. Two closed squares are disjoint iff no vertex of either lies
  in the other and no edges meet; containment is checked per corner.
- `./verify_all.sh` runs both on all 321 certificates in about 2 minutes on one core. All pass. The minimum certified
  clearance is about 1e-20 (pairs) and 5e-21 (walls).
- `./reproduce.sh` re-solves each input with `exactsolve.py` and compares the regenerated certificate byte for byte;
  about 1–2 CPU-hours for all 321.

**What the checkers share.** Same author and agent, and the same certificate parser conventions. The geometry code is
separate (face-normal SAT vs. polygon intersection). Neither shares code with the solver that produced the certificates,
except that `exactsolve.py` calls `verify_cert.py` on its own output.

**Not done.**
- The certificates prove only the upper bounds. That each `S` is a local minimum is numerical evidence, not an
  interval proof: an 80-digit KKT point; multipliers λ ≥ 0 from an LP; reduced Hessian PSD modulo exact flat motions,
  checked in f64; and a first-order MILP test over corner–corner disjunctions. On that evidence 315 of the 321 are
  KKT local minima, 44 of the 48 improvements among them. Six are certified bounds only (n = 177, 211, 230, 261, 263,
  272).
- n = 105, 130 and 292 are not certified; the solver could not find a consistent contact set. At n = 105 the witness
  has an equilibrium residual of 1e-3, and our MILP finds a first-order descent (−2.8e-6 per unit step) once
  corner–corner touches may slip. So it may not be a local minimum, but we have not resolved it.
- No closed forms or minimal polynomials for the 48.

**Lineage and credit.** The packings are their finders'. 46 of the 48 are Francisco Couzo's
(franciscouzo/square-packing); n = 126 and 211 are Joost de Winter's. The method is the same as David
Ellsworth's analytic minimisation (contact equations plus stationarity, his nested Jacobian-determinant conditions). It
is reimplemented as a high-precision KKT Newton solve with the rational certificate added. Register data: CC BY 4.0,
Joshua Levy, the squares project. The local clone is from 3 October, plus the frontier files and 10 witnesses that
changed by 5 October.

**AI assistance.** The solver, verifiers and this batch were written with Claude (Anthropic) as a coding and research agent, directed and reviewed by me.

For n = 17, please treat the exact form from #419 as the object, not the rational certificate from this issue. The exact form implies the certificate's bound, and we withdraw S' for n = 17 as a separate submission. Everything below is pinned to commit [8c47162](https://github.com/evand/square-packing/tree/8c47162cec22f02791abfbf7dedb8094de91189a).

- **Exact form:** `search/exact/minpoly/data/n-17.minpoly.json.gz`, SHA-256 `1f81bbe54c9763650b00479bc649a6ec66954816ff277ae43dafa756c3b02a42`. S* is the unique root, in a rational interval of width 2·10⁻³⁷, of an irreducible integer polynomial p of degree 18. The configuration is exact over a number field of degree 18. The packing is John Bidwell's (1997), the register's record. The construction is his; the file is its exact KKT point.
- **Independent check:** `python3 search/exact/verify_exact.py search/exact/minpoly/data/n-17.minpoly.json.gz` uses only the standard library and takes about 2 s. It prints `VALID`: 60 touching incidences are proved as identities in the field, 360 strict inequalities by rational interval arithmetic, and 99 pairs by disjoint discs.
- **Lean:** `lean/Sqpack/Exact/Batch/N17.lean` (with `N17/Data.lean` and `N17/C0.lean`). Its theorem `packs : ∃ s : ℝ, peval pS s = 0 ∧ Sa ≤ s ∧ s ≤ Sb ∧ Packs 17 s` binds the polynomial, the selected root and the configuration in one statement. It is kernel-checked with the standard axioms only, and was rebuilt today with `search/exact/lean_batch.py --maxdeg 20 --only 17` (187 s). The generic step is `packs_exact` in `lean/Sqpack/ExactCheck.lean`.
- **Relation to the rational certificate here:** S' = 233776504680227547584043328571/5·10²⁸ lies about 5·10⁻²⁰ above the interval's upper end Sb, so `Packs 17 S'` follows from `packs` by monotonicity (`packs_of_le`). Neither S' nor S* improves the register's 4.67553009360455; it is the same packing, exactly.

**Coordination — October 9, 2026:** Overall research tracker: #405. Current certificate
roster: #413; the original two classes: #358; verifier tooling: #400. The report below
records the contributor’s branching-rule measurements and plans.
Faster production remains distinct from standing FULL replay and ledger admission; this
producer workstream stays open.

* * *

Follow-up to #350 and #358, on the cost of the sub-pattern branch and bound in
`devtools/pilot_n17_subpattern_bb.py`.

## What is measured

All figures are full runs to certified-infeasible, with the same relaxation and the same
outward-rounded `dual_bound` checks as the pilot.
Only the choice of which square’s angle to split changes.

Branching rule ("B2"): every time a node is closed, the pairs that carry its closing
certificate (the pairs with non-zero Farkas multipliers, or the disc / pair test that
closed it) add weight to both of their squares.
An angle split then takes the square with the largest weight, ties broken by the number
of overlapping pairs at the centre angle and then by width.
Pair splits are unchanged.
“B2d” adds a decay: each new contribution weighs 1.1 times the previous one.

| class | current rule | B2 | B2d |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| A (6 interior cells) | 41,958 | 30,822 | 30,822 |
| side-S0, side-N0 + 5 interior | ≈ 2.17 M | 194,328 | 131,327 |
| side-S0, side-W0 + 5 interior | ≈ 1.10 M | 79,396 | 47,193 |

(nodes; the current-rule runs on the two flagged classes are from #358’s screen.)

- The certificate format does not change, and the standing branch-and-bound verifier
  accepts splits at any point of an interval.
  The B2 certificate for side-S0, side-W0 + 5 interior has been rechecked in full by
  that verifier (37 min on one process).
- An independent implementation of the same weighting in a separate prover also closes
  both classes.
- With the native kernel from #350, one process takes 2–3 minutes for these classes.
- A separate Rust checker, written from the verifier’s specification without the
  producer’s code, passes A’s certificate in 90 s, against 1,550 s for the standing
  verifier. Corrupted certificates (multipliers, bounds, cut right-hand sides, branches)
  are rejected by both at the same check.

## What we are working on

- Certificates for the two classes of #358 with B2, and their full checks by the
  standing verifier.
- Rerunning all 88 flagged classes, flag 2, W7 and SW9 with B2d, under increasing time
  limits.
- Before we certify a smaller sub-pattern, we run a numerical search for a placement.
  One candidate (side-S0, side-S1, interior-SW, interior-NW, interior-W, interior-N)
  turned out to be feasible, with a placement checked exactly.

We will open PRs for the branching rule and the checker when they are ready.

Why the trees shrink, as far as we can tell from the dives:

- In most flagged classes the contradiction lives among a few squares along a wall. The current rule picks the square to split by geometric criteria (width, overlapping pairs), so it also refines squares that never appear in the closing certificates. Each such split roughly doubles the tree without bringing the contradiction closer.
- With the current rule, random dives on the heavy classes end at depth ≈ 25 (log2 of the node count). With B2 they end at depth 12–14, about the depth of an independent prover that shrinks the centre boxes at every node.
- The weights point the splits at the squares that the dual certificates actually use. The decay in B2d lets the choice follow the part of the tree being explored, much like activity scores with decay in SAT solvers (VSIDS).

The rule only chooses where to split. Whether a node closes is decided by the same outward-rounded `dual_bound` check, so soundness is unchanged.

Both classes are now certified, and both certificates pass the standing verifier in full mode.

| Class | Nodes | Closed leaves | Max depth | Certificate (gzip objects) | Standing verifier (full, one process) | Independent Rust check |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| side-S0, side-N0, interior-SW, interior-NW, interior-W, interior-S, interior-SE | 194,328 | 97,563 | 39 | 391 objects, 287,584,492 bytes | PASS, 5,906 s | PASS, 173 s (4 threads) |
| side-S0, side-W0, interior-SW, interior-NW, interior-W, interior-S, interior-SE | 79,396 | 40,224 | 32 | 161 objects, 112,191,343 bytes | PASS, 2,220 s | PASS, 68 s (4 threads) |

**What changed from the plan: the branching rule.** The trees above come from a different choice of which angle to bisect (B2). The judgement is unchanged:

- every closure and every bound move still passes the outward-rounded `dual_bound`;
- the certificate format is unchanged, and the standing verifier reads it without modification.

The standing verifier accepts any split point inside the parent interval, so the rule affects only the shape of the tree.

The pilot’s default rule needs about 2.17 million nodes on the first class and about 1.10 million on the second. We generated the second one with the default rule as well. Its certificate passed the independent Rust check, but its standing-verifier run needed about 7.9 GB and was killed when the host ran out of memory. With B2 the two trees are about 11 and 14 times smaller, and the standing verifier fits comfortably.

**The rule (B2).**

- **Learning.** Every node closed by the LP passes each positive Farkas multiplier’s share `y / sum(y)` to both squares of the pair that owns that row. Cell and wall rows pass nothing. A node closed by `disc` or `pair` adds 1 to both squares of that pair. The weights accumulate over the whole run.
- **Choosing a pair split.** Pair splits are chosen exactly as in the pilot.
- **Choosing an angle split.** Among the squares whose angle interval is at least `split_ratio` (0.25) of the widest, bisect the one with the largest learned weight; ties go to the wider interval. Until any weight exists, the score is the number of pairs that overlap at the LP centres with every angle at its interval midpoint.

On pattern A the same rule gives 30,822 nodes against 41,958 for the default rule. That certificate also passes the independent Rust check.

A variant, B2d, discounts old weight by a factor of 1.1 per closure. It reduces the trees a further 32 to 41 per cent (131,327 and 47,193 nodes). We kept B2 for these certificates, so that the rule here matches what was measured first. #367 tracks the rule work.

**Why the side cells are needed.** Removing either side cell from either class leaves a pattern that can be packed: side-S0, side-N0 or side-W0 together with the five interior cells, and also the five interior cells alone. For each of these four patterns we found a placement numerically and checked it exactly over the rationals. We have not tested removing an interior cell.

**Reproducing.**

- The rule is a small optional module that wraps `devtools.n17_bb_native` (about 200 lines). It changes only `Solver.children`, and for B2 it wraps `Solver.assess` to collect the multipliers.
- We will open it as a pull request together with the native recording path, so that the certificates can be regenerated from this repository. Until then, the rule as described above is enough to check the claim, because the standing verifier checks the tree it is given and does not depend on how the tree was chosen.
- Regenerating with the module gives byte-identical certificates. We checked this for the second class (same SHA-256 over all objects) and for A.

**Hosting (OR-18).** The certificate objects are release assets of [wand125/n17-certificates](https://github.com/wand125/n17-certificates), tag [`b2-classes-20261005`](https://github.com/wand125/n17-certificates/releases/tag/b2-classes-20261005). The hosted-data manifest entries (path, asset, size and SHA-256 for each of the 391 and 161 objects) are in `b2-classes/` on its main branch, and every uploaded asset matches them. We can add the entries with the ledger entry in a pull request here, or move the assets to a release of this repository if you prefer that.
