body:
Umbrella issue for the n = 11 optimality result (T-060, `s(11) = T`): the proof imported from [Queuingtheorydotcom/11SquaresOptimal](https://github.com/Queuingtheorydotcom/11SquaresOptimal/tree/f9e0de713a0949d1bc6a0fa6b59d96edf6c3d65c), the Squares Project's confirmation and explainer paper, the two adversarial reviews of October 3, the deltas those produced on the original, and what should go back to the contributor and into the formalization effort. The sections below are the summary as of October 3, 2026; the record for the contributor is `docs/project/reviews/review-2026-10-03-n11-optimality-upstream-delta.md`, in [jlevy/squares#318](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/pull/318).

## Where things stand

- **The paper** ([A Review of the Optimality Proof of the Trump Packing of 11 Squares](https://jlevy.github.io/squares/papers/n11-optimality-review.md)) is at **v0.1.3**. Source: `packing/devtools/templates/n11-optimality-review-article.md`; history in `packing/src/sqpack/release.py`.
- **T-060 stands at S5/V3/C3**: machine certificate replayed here, review record pending on both axes under the ladder of 2026-09-30. No fresh single run of the whole global corpus has been made; the composer checks retained joins. Neither distinct-method confirmation nor formalization is claimed.
- **Merged:** [jlevy/squares#313](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/pull/313) (both adversarial reviews applied as v0.1.1 and v0.1.2, four retained components, GPT-6 Pro's evidence pack, portable replay commands) and [jlevy/squares#314](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/pull/314) (v0.1.3 closing section on receipts, the receipts register, the review file renamed "unified").
- **Records:** `docs/project/reviews/review-2026-10-03-n11-optimality-paper-adversarial.md` (the project's own review), `docs/project/reviews/review-2026-10-03-n11-optimality-adversarial-gpt6-pro-unified.md` (GPT-6 Pro's, filed verbatim), `docs/project/reviews/review-2026-10-03-n11-gpt6-pro-review-integration.md` (one row per finding with its disposition), `packing/resources/web/n11-optimality-2026-09-29/receipts/README.md` (the receipts register), `packing/resources/web/n11-optimality-gpt6-pro-review-2026-10-03/` (the evidence pack, 196 of 202 files, 5.4 MB, restorable byte for byte).
- **Beads:** epic `think-1gbu` with three open children: `think-if2i` (semantic parent admission), `think-nnrx` (upstream items for the contributor), `think-wbpu` (independent global kernel); `think-rt86` (register and v0.1.3) closed.

## What the two reviews established

Neither review, nor the integration, found a counterexample or a fatal error. Every number the paper states was reproduced, most by independent recomputation (exact arithmetic in Q(u), the cover and overlay rebuilt, all 46 field transfer sets, all 8,448 dual margins from first principles), and every retained receipt that can run in this checkout replays with zero non-timing differences.

## The delta on the imported proof

**Corrections to statements (applied in the paper; the original's wording is the contributor's to fix):**

1. The pose-preservation invariant is stated row by row: for every row whose angle interval contains the owner's actual angle, the owner's actual center lies in that row's polygon, and the rows cover the angular range. This is what justifies dropping a row's single shared angle at a seam; the union statement does not. The implementation already enforced it.
2. Ownership is quantified over valid packings, not over the artificial poses a loose outer cover retains; the original's section 5 reads the stronger way.
3. Each separation feature is a conjunction over four corners, and the pair condition is a disjunction over the eight features; one negative corner disables the feature.
4. The field citation: the original's section 5 contains no charge lemma. The lemma (definition, capacity one, whole-angle lower bound, transfer by O ⊆ J with Σ q > b, applied to J or its half-turn, strict budget) lives in the paper, cited to the original's section 12 for the 59 certificates and the transfer rule.
5. The historical closed-interval helper `covers_vertical` falsely accepts a singleton target against intervals below it: 616 of 12,180 cases in the control, all singletons, none in the other direction. Its use stays sound because every caller sweeps a full-dimensional convex domain, whose interior slices have positive length, and a finite union of closed regions contains their limits; zero-area domains are refused or sent to an exact point-and-segment check. A corrected kernel exists for new callers (`packing/devtools/n11_closed_interval_cover.py`).
6. Four final-state digests in the publisher's leaf audits are stale (far15 `3b7f1ea0` → observed `9e28b092`, far13 `f83eb23c` → `87482985`, far2 `7551646f` → `11d4a28e`, near `81002706` → `a6d45c0c`). The near object was verified at 185,901,535 decoded bytes. This is a release defect, not a geometric one.
7. The worked mask-0 row (cell 1, row 0, angle interval [0, 1/64]): the accepted proposal covers it with the feature region and four owned points of squares 0 and 2; two points already suffice. The review's three-point list was correct but neither minimal nor what the proposal records.

**Simplifications, each with evidence in the repository:**

8. One closing contact (squares 2 and 10) defines the polynomial p(u) = 5u⁸ − 10u⁷ − 2u⁶ + 14u⁵ + 12u⁴ − 6u³ + 2u² + 2u − 1, and p' > 4 on [9/25, 37/100] certifies the root unique there (minimum of p' above 4.32).
9. The local isolation lemma in weighted-residual form: η = Σ r_k |e_k|, and the certificate condition η + M_j/2 < r_j; the checker's coarser bound ε_j R gives the accepted margin and the ratio c_j Figure 10 draws. The two ratio conventions are different numbers.
10. **Two-radius box:** r = 1/256 for every coordinate, 1/128 for the angles of squares 9 and 10; six curvature constants K/r² (pairs 21/2, 57/4, 99/4, 30; walls 3/4, 3). The unchanged isolation audit, run through a wrapper that pins the variant, passes with worst ratio 0.8667 under the repository's finer bounds (0.9515 under the six constants alone), all 128 branches and 8,448 margins; every accepted radius is at most its replacement (tightest 0.904). Receipt: `receipts/local-isolation-two-radius/`.
11. **Incidence propagation** replaces the final D4 search: 648 source-triple combinations, with 168/47/1, 198/17/1 and 196/20/0 immediate contradictions, survivors after propagation, and survivors after forcing for sources 999, 1462 and 1659; the one survivor has the owners of cells 1 and 2 in overlay regions inside [23/50, 27/50] × [0, 11/100] and [11/25, 14/25] × [23/100, 7/25], and (U − 1)²((1/10)² + (7/25)²) < 1989/2500 < 1 closes it; the 1462 survivor is the reflection of the 999 one. Receipt: `receipts/d4-incidence/`.
12. **Minimal field selection:** of the 46 accepted field packets, 44 are mandatory and already cover all 1,904 field cases, so the minimum is 44 and unique; the review's 43 + 1 counts a publisher packet not retained here. Manifest: `receipts/field-batch-a/minimal-selection.json`. Nothing deleted.
13. The ten-hull form of the five-site charge (the core meets the convex hull of every three of the five sites), with the no-site example: sites (±1/2, 0), (0, ±1/2), (1/2, 1/2), core [−3/10, 3/10]².
14. The uniqueness corollary, conditional on the same exclusion and capture ensemble: every optimal packing is the construction up to the eight symmetries and relabeling. The project registers only optimality.
15. Examined and found unavailable: a D4-symmetric sixteen-cell cover (best grid 0.3536 normalized against 0.3476 required). Radius headroom: scaling the fitted radii by 1.2 gives worst ratio 0.81, by 1.4 gives 0.95, by 1.5 the argument fails.

**Interfaces made explicit (in the paper):** the frame and unit legend; the role bijection from construction squares to case-438 cells [3, 15, 8, 0, 4, 1, 2, 11, 9, 10, 13]; the 33 radii and the sixteen cover sites as exact integers over 2,000,000, generated from the receipts; the four closed branches versus the ten-node ancestry; the scope notice beside the theorem; what a receipt is and the three verification depths (hash integrity, retained composition, fresh geometry per component).

**Reproduction:** the validation guide carries portable commands for every retained checker with declared inputs, outputs and ceilings; each was run verbatim and matched its receipt apart from timing. Still not reproducible here: pose inclusion needs the 185.9 MB near object (Git LFS, pinned), and the capture nodes need the publisher's source states and byte-exact parent receipts.

## For the contributor (`think-nnrx`)

- Publish a corrected immutable release with the four digests rebound and an old-to-new binding report.
- State the pointwise angular-row invariant and valid-packing ownership in section 5, and add the charge lemma the paper now carries.
- Consider adopting upstream, as simplifications of the published proof: the two-radius box with six constants, the incidence bridge in place of the 1,572-ban search, and the 44-certificate selection in place of 59.

## Suggestions for the formalization

Ordered so that each step is a closed statement with its own finite certificate, and the trust base shrinks at each.

1. **Endpoint and construction first.** Everything is in Q(u) with p(u) above: the root's uniqueness on [9/25, 37/100], the 44 vertex containments and 55 pair separations as exact sign conditions, T = (6u + 4)/(1 + 2u − u²) and the rational cap U with U − T ≈ 2.1 × 10⁻²¹, and the opposite-wall span deduction that turns S < U into S < T. This is the smallest unit and the one a proof assistant can take whole.
2. **State the capture proposition as a quantified sentence**, over every valid packing with S ≤ T, naming the allowed symmetries and relabelings, the closed branches, the source and target frames and the target rectangle. The formal proof then needs verified checkers for four closed rules (pose update, ownership, charge, closed cover), not the search programs that proposed the certificates.
3. **Formalize the row-by-row invariant, not the union**, with the seam rule as its corollary, and ownership quantified over valid packings. Formalize the corrected closed-interval contract (a singleton is covered when some closed interval contains it) and the full-dimensional closure argument once as a lemma; do not formalize the historical predicate.
4. **Take the incidence-propagation bridge rather than the UNSAT search**: 648 records, 220 closed regions, one distance bound, versus 1,572 bans and three finite searches.
5. **Take the two-radius box and the weighted-residual lemma**: uniform radii, six rational constants and one abstract lemma replace 33 fitted radii and per-pair curvature bounds; the 8,448 margin checks remain but with simpler inputs and no float anywhere.
6. **Use the ten-hull form of the five-site charge**: a finite statement about convex hulls of three points, easier to formalize than the median projection, and equivalent to it.
7. **Take the 44-certificate selection** as the field obligation, and record the dependency closure it carries.
8. **Define the node state canonically** (assumptions, angle intervals, center domains, owned hulls, roles, frame, scale, rule version) so the formal object is the state and its transition, not a receipt's bytes; this is `think-if2i`, and it is also what a one-command fresh run of the whole ensemble needs.
9. **Keep the composition explicit**: the theorem is the composition of seven obligations (endpoint, exhaustive classification, 2,180 exclusions, reduction to case 438, capture, local isolation and inclusion, the rigid embedding), each with its receipt; a formalization should mirror that table and discharge each row separately.
10. **Independent kernel**: an independent closed-set and transition kernel on the bound source objects (`think-wbpu`) would give the distinct-method confirmation the ladder's higher rungs ask for, and is the natural companion to a formal development.

## Open here

- `think-if2i`: semantic parent admission for the capture receipts.
- `think-wbpu`: the independent global kernel.
- `think-nnrx`: the upstream items above.
- The seven tbd policy grants left unanswered by the 0.10.0 upgrade.
- Naming the revising agent in the paper's credits.

comments.body:
Thanks for the explainer and the list. We cross-checked v0.1.3 against our Lean formalization data and found a few small points:

1. **Formalization status.** The paper says no proof-assistant formalization is claimed (around line 1122). Lean 4 formalizations of this proof are in progress in [wand125/n11-optimality-lean](https://github.com/wand125/n11-optimality-lean) and [Queuingtheorydotcom/11SquaresFormalized](https://github.com/Queuingtheorydotcom/11SquaresFormalized). Some components are already kernel-checked with only the standard axioms, for example the 173 returned cases (independently replayed against Fan's assembly in Queuingtheorydotcom/11SquaresFormalized#7) and the 76 prior cases. You may want to mention them.
2. **Number of root updates.** The text says the root has 14 further updates, but in the published data the 14th stage is `complete = false` (truncated), so 13 updates completed.
3. **Figure 8 vs. the text.** The note under Figure 8 says the exhaustive 1,572-ban search is a separate obligation, while the text says a single ban suffices. A sentence saying which one is intended would help.

One remark on dependencies: our prior-family proof covers all 76 prior cases directly, without assuming the 1,931 baseline cases, so cases 2175 and 2176 do not need that premise there.

All the other figures we compared (U, the 220 regions, the final distance inequality 0.732 < 1989/2500, the 136 near-state rows, the Appendix C corner radii) match our data.

@wand125, your comment of 4 October is answered in v0.1.4 of the paper (#343), each point checked against the retained packet before the text changed. The current edition is v0.1.5.

1. **Formalization status.** The section on what was verified names [wand125/n11-optimality-lean](https://github.com/wand125/n11-optimality-lean) and [Queuingtheorydotcom/11SquaresFormalized](https://github.com/Queuingtheorydotcom/11SquaresFormalized), and reports, attributed to you, that the 76 prior-family and the 173 returned cases are kernel-checked with the standard axioms only. It says this project has reviewed neither formalization and that T-060's rungs do not rest on them. The sentence that no proof-assistant formalization is claimed stays.
2. **Root updates.** The text now says the root node completes thirteen further updates, not fourteen, and that the fourteenth step covers only part of its angle range and changes no ownership; the retained capture receipts hold thirteen complete updates and a fourteenth that is partial.
3. **Figure 8.** The caption and the text now agree: the symmetry lemma rests on the exhaustive assignment search over the 220 regions and 1,572 bans, and the shorter one-ban proof is checked beside it and is not a premise.
4. **Cases 2175 and 2176.** The paragraph says the 1,931-case premise is a premise of those two cases' accepted certificates, and reports your Lean proof of all 76 prior-family cases, which does not use it.

T-060 stays at S5/V3/C3, and its register entry gains a dated note naming both formalizations. Nothing from your comment is still open.

On `main`: [the record of the changes](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/docs/project/reviews/review-2026-10-04-n11-optimality-paper-v0.1.4-changes.md), the [paper's source](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/packing/devtools/templates/n11-optimality-review-article.md) and [`RESULTS.md`](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/packing/frontier/RESULTS.md).

On 6 October @ManassehA06 (Queuingtheorydotcom on GitHub) [announced](https://x.com/ManassehA06/status/2107508501610217640) that the optimality of the 11-square packing "has been formalized in lean thanks to Astra and Claude", and [this project's post](https://x.com/ojoshe/status/2107513739222380935) gives context and shares the announcement. The formalization is [Queuingtheorydotcom/11SquaresFormalized](https://github.com/Queuingtheorydotcom/11SquaresFormalized), and it is now in the record, pinned at `cdc746ed907d258057c283aeb6d077cb2c27e349`. Its acknowledgements credit Queuingtheorydotcom, EvolvingPrograms and @ctjlewis, @wand125, Benjamin Gurevitch, @Julian-JJ and @Guzhou0806.

**What we checked**
- **The statement.** `ElevenSquare.optimality` states T-060's claim: `s(11) = T`, with T the register's exact endpoint `(6u+4)/(1+2u-u^2)`, for closed unit squares with independent rotations, boundary contact allowed and disjoint open interiors. We read the definitions line by line. We also built the 18-module statement closure here on Lean 4.34.1 and Mathlib `d13f23b7`, and checked in Lean that `Optimality` is `IsLeast {S | Packable 11 S} T` and that `T` and the polynomial match term for term. In that build, Trump's packing at side T (`construction_packable`) is kernel-checked using only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`.
- **The axioms.** Your final audit, pinned here by SHA-256, says that `ElevenSquare.optimality` depends on `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` and 13,308 `native_decide` axioms from 10,464 numerical declarations. That is the trust model your README states, `lean_kernel_and_native_compiler`: the proof trusts Lean's compiler as well as its kernel. The prior and returned certificate targets in this integrated snapshot are decided natively too, with 1,832 and 3,920 such axioms, whereas wand125's 4 October note describes kernel-only versions of those components.
- **The source tree.** A streamed read of the commit's archive matched the SHA-256 of all 7,920 modules to your final audit. A scan of every module found no `sorry`, no `axiom` declaration, no `implemented_by`, `extern` or `unsafe`, and no notation or macro. The only escape it found is the `native_decide` you document.

**Where it stands**
- **T-060's rungs.** T-060 stays at V3/C3. The full 7,920-module build was not repeated here: this host cannot hold the roughly 8 GB of compiled objects. Run 37414883750 is in a private repository, so the record holds your run as the source's report.
- **What rung 5 needs.** A complete build that the record can rest on, either run here from the pin or a third party's build retained here, and a review of the formalization by a named human Lean expert who is not one of its authors.
- **Three stale texts.** Some texts at the pin still call the bound conditional or pending: the doc-comments of `Optimality.lean` and `Pending/S09_GlobalLowerBound.lean`, and `verification/admissions.json` (`SOURCE_COMPLETE_REPLAY_PENDING`). Your final audit's axiom map says otherwise, so you may want to update them.

The record: [the statement audit](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/docs/project/reviews/review-2026-10-06-n11-lean-formalization-statement-audit.md), [the adversarial review](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/docs/project/reviews/review-2026-10-06-n11-lean-formalization-adversarial.md), [the retained packet](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/packing/resources/web/queuingtheorydotcom-n11-lean-2026-10-06/README.md) and T-060 in [`RESULTS.md`](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/packing/frontier/RESULTS.md).
